text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression on small-batch text-gen after the autotune roll (deploy at ~1798100000). Short requests (<=64 tokens) are ~10–15% slower in p50 and p95. Repro on both gpu-rt and cpu-rt. cc @marta @kevin

marta: Which kernel/path is the runtime picking for seq_len=32? Shortctx should hit the lightweight attention path.

alex: Autotuner flipped to use merged-attn-v2 for a lot of seq_len buckets. The autotune scoring favored it because the microbench was using batch sizes 16–64. In prod, most shortctx requests are batch=1–4, so merged-attn-v2 is slower there.

kevin: Can you paste the autotune output and the per-bucket profiler lines that show the decision?

alex: Sure — here's the relevant snippet from the tuner's logfile and the perf dump: 

```
# autotune picks (excerpt)
bucket(seq=32): candidates=[merged-attn-v2, fused-prefill, small-attn],
  scores({batch=32}): {merged-attn-v2:0.92, fused-prefill:0.89, small-attn:0.71}
  scores({batch=1}):  {merged-attn-v2:0.78, fused-prefill:0.95, small-attn:0.82}
choose_kernel -> merged-attn-v2 (based on avg-score across tuning samples)

# profiler trace (production sampled)
2026-03-16T14:02:11Z choose_kernel: bucket=seq32, batch=1 -> merged-attn-v2
2026-03-16T14:02:11Z kernel_exec time(ms): merged-attn-v2=9.8, fused-prefill=6.1
2026-03-16T14:02:12Z kv_cache_lookup(ms)=0.12, kv_apply(ms)=0.33
```

alex: So autotune aggregated over the tuning set (which had heavy large-batch traffic) and picked the candidate that wins at scale but loses for our common small-batch shortctx path.

rachel: Two options: (1) make buckets include batch-size dimension (seq_len x batch) and autotune each, or (2) keep coarse buckets but change autotune scoring to weight p50/p95 for sampled batch sizes matching live distribution (i.e., weight batch=1 more). I prefer (2) as it's less combinatorial.

marta: Also we need hysteresis in kernel selection to avoid flip-flopping when diff is tiny. Last time flips increased jitter. Suggest: require >=6% improvement sustained over N tuning rounds OR a weighted latency delta with batch-aware weighting.

kevin: Agree. Quick mitigation: add workload-aware weighting and a safety threshold. Patch suggestion (runtime config):

```
runtime.autotune = {
  sample_weights = {batch=1:0.6, batch=2:0.2, batch>=4:0.2},
  decision_hysteresis_pct = 6,
  min_samples = 200,
  fallback_on_p95_regression = true
}
```

kevin: If we flip this flag to `weighted_by_workload_v2` on the canary pool that serves shortctx heavy traffic, we should see merged-attn-v2 drop out for seq_len<=64.

perf-bot: Canary run results (A/B split, 2h):
- control (master autotune): p50=6.8ms, p95=18.2ms
- weighted_by_workload_v2: p50=5.9ms (-13%), p95=13.9ms (-23%)
- CPU util diff: -8% on canary nodes

alex: Nice. Those numbers match local profiling. I'll open a PR with the config changes + a small change in the autotune scorer to include batch-weighted p95. PR will include perf traces and the canary run logs.

marta: Once PR is up, let's roll to staging and run longer (6–12h) to be safe. Also add a trace id to sample selection so we can correlate misroutes.

kevin: For longer-term: consider adding a lightweight online learner to adapt picks if production distribution drifts (but gated behind safe rollback). For now we'll stick to config change.

alex: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2483 (draft). Attaching perf artifacts there.

rachel: Thanks — set the rollout flag on canary and ping infra to do a slow ramp if metrics stay good. :thumbsup: 

alex: Will do. Filing a follow-up ticket to track seq_len x batch autotuning exploration (ENG-RT-682).

marta: Great, thanks for catching this early.

kevin: LGTM once CI passes.

perf-bot: Note: regression alert cleared after canary flip at 1798122000.

alex: Closing loop here — I'll post post-mortem if anything unexpected shows up in the next 24h.
